### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `71b0adfe0ee4b5d16a335747a254e1dcabd5af10` — the merge of head `dd5521040e2ba6c6ae9873c8cdc8649ec68ece4e` into base `50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 71b0adfe0ee4b5d16a335747a254e1dcabd5af10 && git checkout 71b0adfe0ee4b5d16a335747a254e1dcabd5af10
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7 dd5521040e2ba6c6ae9873c8cdc8649ec68ece4e && git checkout -B drift-repro 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7 && git merge --no-ff dd5521040e2ba6c6ae9873c8cdc8649ec68ece4e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 50e35a280994dcecb714b6fa1f2d44840900f5e7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dd5521040e2ba6c6ae9873c8cdc8649ec68ece4e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts, scripts/check-stack-collection-maps.mjs, packages/metadata/src/owner-stamp-residual-build-boot.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/manifest-service-residual-objects.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-collection-item-owner-stamp.test.ts + packages/spec/src/kernel/collection-item-owner-stamp.ts, packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-plugin.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/meta-spelling/manifest-collection-spelling.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts, packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts, packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/view-container-names.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts, packages/core/src/metadata-service-contract.ts, docs/adr/0130-release-artifact-as-co-ownership-boundary.md, docs/adr/0010-metadata-protection-model.md, docs/adr/0021-analytics-dataset-semantic-layer.md

Inputs: card #29518 (body and all six comments), PR #29593 (body, file list, `git diff origin/main...dd552104` at merge base `ff827bcf`), and the check-runs on the head, read twice (20:36Z and 20:44Z). The changeset is a prose face: judged in ②, not in ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Build-door accept set (`ObjectStackDefinitionSchema`, the owner-stamp refinement).** A `packages[]` stack's top-level `datasets[i]` whose `name` no body's `datasets` claims is now judged as residual: a `_packageId` other than `manifest.id` raises `datasets.i._packageId`. Before, `TOP_LEVEL_COLLECTIONS_NEVER_RESIDUAL` excluded `datasets` and such an item parsed whatever it wore. **Narrowing, right.** The set is a mirror of `unclaimedTopLevel`'s walk, and the walk now carries `datasets`; I took the set difference at head myself: `OWNER_STAMP_JUDGED_COLLECTIONS` minus the keys of `ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE` is exactly `{data, jobs}`, which is what the mirror now holds and what the metadata mirror test pins (`notResidual == ['data', 'jobs']`).
- **Everything else the build door accepts is unchanged.** A package BODY's datasets were already judged (`datasets` sits in `OWNER_STAMP_JUDGED_COLLECTIONS`, both doors); a stack without `packages[]` takes the untouched single-body branch; an unstamped residual dataset parses as before; a top-level dataset a body repeats is a claimed slot and is not judged at the top level. Right.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec`: nothing moves.** `TOP_LEVEL_COLLECTIONS_NEVER_RESIDUAL` is a module-private `const`; at head the only file naming it is `stack.zod.ts` (no api-surface, baseline or generated file). The `minor` is the kind's floor, not a surface move. Right.
- **`@objectstack/metadata` (`ARTIFACT_FIELD_TO_TYPE` gains `datasets: 'dataset'`).** Three consequences, each read in the cited code: (a) `unclaimedTopLevel` lists a residual dataset (slot = `name`, via `artifactItemSlot`); (b) `registerUnclaimedTopLevel` registers it under `manifest.id`/version through `registerArtifactBodyCollections`, whose `artifactItemOwnerStampRefusal` judges the field because it is in the judged set, so a foreign stamp is `VALIDATION_ERROR` 400 at `_packageId`; (c) the artifact door's body loop now also writes every body's datasets into the in-memory loader and the `MetadataManager`, stamped with the body's provenance (`dataset` is a registered type, `loadOrder` 55, before `report`/`dashboard`). (c) is runtime behaviour, not a key an author writes, so folding it under `narrowed` rather than declaring an `added` kind is right (`narrowed` wins the several-kinds rule anyway).
- **`@objectstack/objectql`: no source change needed, and none made.** The engine's residual seam `registerUnclaimedTopLevelItems` is generic (`registerItem(type, …)` for every residual type outside `{object, picklist, object_extension}`), with `collectionItemOwnerStampRefusal` applied first; the body seam's `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS` already carries `datasets` and registers through the same `registerItem('dataset', …)`. So a residual dataset lands in the registry under the stack's id and version, as the new kernel-boot pin asserts (`RELEASE_ID`/`1.0.0` beside the body's `SERVICE_ID`/`2.4.0`, the artifact's own entry left unstamped). Right.
- **No second-writer hazard.** `ObjectQLPlugin.loadMetadataFromService` syncs `object`/`view`/`app`/`flow`/`hook` only, never `dataset`; the protocol's `readFlattenedMetaItems` answers `GET /meta/dataset` from `engine.registry.listItems` plus stored overlays, not from the `MetadataManager`, so the artifact door's new manager copy cannot duplicate the served list on an ObjectQL kernel. That matches the PR's measured "single-package artifact: `/meta/dataset` unchanged; the metadata service's own list went from empty to the body dataset" and makes the sealed (`artifact-only`) runtime the one whose served list changes. Right, and declared in the changeset.
- **CLI readers of the residual rule.** `view-container-names.ts` keeps only `type === 'view'` residual items; `picklist-references.ts` reads only residual picklists. A residual dataset adds no `os validate` / `os build` finding beyond the schema's own stamp issue. Right.
- **First consumer.** `packages/rest/src/analytics-routes.ts` resolves `body.datasetName` through `getMetaItems({ type: 'dataset' })` and answers 404 `NOT_FOUND` otherwise. That is the card's run-time failure far from the cause; with the dataset registered under the stack's id it is found. Right.
- **`scripts/check-stack-collection-maps.mjs`.** With the map entry present, a `missing` waiver naming `datasets` is stale and the gate reds stale waivers, so the key had to leave the row. The row's sentence now holds for the three keys that remain (AppPlugin does schedule `jobs` and read `datasources`/`translations` off the bundle) and says why `datasets` was never the same fact: every "datasets" AppPlugin reads is a seed dataset (`data:`, `readSeedDatasets`/`mergeSeedDatasets`), never the ADR-0021 kind. Right.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/29518-residual-top-level-datasets.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/metadata: minor`. Both publish (neither `package.json` is private, both at 18.2.0). The kind is `narrowed`, which takes at least `minor` on each package the diff moves. `@objectstack/objectql` moves only a test file and `scripts/` is not a package, so no third entry is owed. One file for two packages is a legal changeset. **Matches the diff.**
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, one arm from the closed pair. The diff refuses a value that used to parse (a foreign `_packageId` on a residual dataset), which is the definition of `narrowed`, and it widens no authorable surface, so `no` with the `(narrowing)` arm is the right declaration and the face this record stands on. The ADR-0087 marker is present exactly once, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and the body carries the fix in writing (drop the stamp, or declare the dataset inside its owner's `packages[]` entry). No conversion could rewrite ownership, and a stack carrying such an item lost the dataset at boot before, so no working stored state is preserved by a migration. **Disposition holds.**
- Check-runs: the first `Check Changeset` run on the head concluded `failure` (level axis: `narrowed` beside a `Clause-②: no` with no arm) because it read the PR body before the body edit that added the arm; the superseding run on the same head concluded `success`. The gate's standing verdict on this head is the later one.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev report 6587764387: `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `premise_still_valid: true`. Deviations: one changeset file carrying both packages (allowed, both names and levels read) and the report signed with the dispatching seat's lane (cosmetic). **Answered.**
- `out_of_scope_findings`: `jobs`, `datasources`, `translations` stay on the waiver row, not measured here. Not a defect of this change and not a contract violation; the row's sentence is now accurate for those three. **Answered, no card owed.**
- **Escalated, should-fix (prose, non-blocking):** the PR body's "No dogfood run: no `!` in the title and no `(narrowing)` arm on the Clause-② line" and the report's `dogfood_battery: n/a` contradict the body's own `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. The arm was added at the head commit after the first changeset gate reading; the dev skill owes the full dogfood battery once on the final head when the arm is `(narrowing)`. The head's `Dogfood Regression Gate` check-run concluded `success`, so the mechanical reading exists; the sentence in the body is stale and the adopting seat should have it corrected or the local battery recorded.
- Claim chain: claim 6585254964 amended by 6586240516 on triage's cross-domain designation 6585309156, which widened the file surface to `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` and named this review. The diff stays inside the amended surface; `protocol.ts` (frozen) is untouched. Rider 6583740976 (the comment at `owner-stamp-residual-build-boot.test.ts` L173-175) is done in the diff. **Answered.**
- PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay write), head repo equals base repo (not a fork), draft, 100/22 lines, no governed surface in the file list (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success). The schema face alone owes this record.
- Check-runs on the head at 20:47Z (third read): success for `Check Changeset` (superseding run), `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, the three `Lint · scoped` jobs, `Type Check · source gates` / `consumer gates` / `debt ledger`, `Spec property liveness`, `Plan Test Core shards`, `Build UI Deps`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Check PR Size`, `PR-body guards`; the one `failure` is the first `Check Changeset` run superseded above; still `in_progress`: `Test Core` (8 shards), `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI` (16 shards), `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`. The landing waits on the required set going green; this record judges the contract and names the gate state as read.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts`** (schema face; against ADR-0130 D4's residual rule as the code carries it, ADR-0010's one owner-stamp judge, ADR-0021's `dataset` as a registered metadata type, and its first consumer). The mirror's whole contract is to agree with `unclaimedTopLevel` collection by collection; once the door's map carries `datasets`, keeping it in the never-residual set would make the build door accept what the boot refuses, which is the disagreement the metadata mirror test exists to catch (it went red before the spec line, as the PR says, and the reverse verification at the final head is consistent with that). Dropping `datasets` is the only edit that restores the mirror. I checked the three places the mirror could still drift: slot derivation (`residualSlotOf` reads `name`; `artifactItemSlot` reads `name` for every non-view type), owner (`manifest.id` on both sides; `unclaimed.ownerId` falls back to `id` only when `manifest` is absent, where the schema judges against no package in the same way), and the singular spelling (`pluralToSingular('datasets')` is `'dataset'`, the registry type). The docblock now states the two-collection reading correctly (`data` to the seed loader, `jobs` scheduled, both off the merged stack through `resolveArtifactCollections`) and drops the retired "datasets are read off the package bodies only" sentence. Break attempts: a top-level dataset a body repeats stays the body's and is judged nowhere at the top level (CONTROL pin); a residual dataset with no `name` has no slot at either door; a config-door stack parsed with `strict: false` never meets this gate, but `registerUnclaimedTopLevel` and the engine's residual seam both judge it, so no door accepts what the other refuses. **Holds. No must-fix.**

**`packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts`.** One map entry with its reason in place; the map's own gate pins it to the schema in both directions. The "see the end of this map" pointer for the seed `data:` collection is accurate. Making the artifact door the metadata-service registrar of body datasets is a consequence the changeset declares rather than hides. **Holds.**

**`scripts/check-stack-collection-maps.mjs`.** Waiver keys and text track the map; the self-test ran in `Lint · repo & tooling gates` (success). **Holds.**

**The three test files.** The spec pin asserts the issue path `datasets.0._packageId` on a residual dataset and keeps `data`/`jobs` on the never-judged table; the metadata mirror holds the two doors equal and reads `['data', 'jobs']`; the kernel-boot pin registers the residual dataset under the stack's id and version beside a body's own, with the CONTROL for a repeated top-level dataset. These are the right layers. **Should-fix, non-blocking:** no pin names `datasets` at the metadata door's registration (the mirror's sink is a no-op and asserts refusal only; the artifact-boot reading in the PR is a deleted scratch probe). The decision half and the engine door are pinned, and the metadata door's loop is generic over the map, so this is a coverage note, not a hole.
